objective: Create a current, evidence-backed inventory of market-data provider candidates covering the P01-A Crypto, Forex and context universe without selecting a production provider.
scope: Evaluate Forex pricing/tick/bar data sources and their proxy-volume semantics
Evaluate exchange-native futures/context sources for Gold, Oil, USDX and VIX
Record official U.S. Treasury rates source coverage for baseline yield context
Record REST/WebSocket/streaming, market-depth, historical, timestamp/sequence, derivatives and operational characteristics
Record licensing/storage/redistribution questions and documented access/trial/public-data availability
Identify provider-class redundancy and single-provider dependency risks
Create machine-readable provider inventory and comparison matrix
out_of_scope: Select or rank a production winner
Create provider accounts, subscriptions or API credentials
Enable Demo, Shadow, Live or Auto Trading
tests: Each provider candidate has a unique provider_id
Every factual capability claim has provider/official source references
Crypto and Forex provider coverage are separately modeled
Exchange-native sources are distinguished from aggregators/vendors
Forex volume coverage never implies consolidated global Spot FX volume
Licensing/storage/redistribution fields preserve unknown/TBD rather than inventing rights
No production provider selection or ranking is recorded
security_tests: No live market connection or trading activation
No production-provider authority implied by inventory
evidence: Current provider/exchange official documentation retrieved during task
rollback: Revert P01-B research artifacts and state/catalog reconciliation only. No provider accounts, credentials or runtime changes are created.
definition_of_done: Provider inventory covers the baseline Crypto, Forex and context universe
Provider classes and redundancy risks are documented
Open licensing/compliance/cost questions are explicitly handed to later P01 workstreams
Task Catalog and Current State are reconciled
